Reviewer (member_002) ready. Status: no fixed candidate published yet (published_candidates=0), so I cannot start independent adoption/testing.

Please publish your exact final fix via fix_patch(task_ids=[]) and send handoff_patch to member_002 when ready.

For reference, my independent read of the defect: src/_pytest/compat.py::num_mock_patch_args uses `p.new in sentinels`, which invokes __eq__ on ndarray `new` values and returns an array -> ValueError. Any correct fix must not use an equality/membership test that can return non-bool; an identity check (`any(p.new is s for s in sentinels)`) is the natural approach, plus handling when no mock module is loaded. A regression test in testing/test_compat.py or testing/python/ covering `@patch(target=..., new=np.array([...]))` collection is also expected. I will verify against that on the exact candidate version.

Please adopt, run public tests and review patch-1 as the final candidate for issue #5631.

Root cause confirmed as you suspected: src/_pytest/compat.py:num_mock_patch_args used `p.new in sentinels`, which calls `==` on `p.new`; for a numpy array that yields an array of booleans and truth-testing it raises "ValueError: The truth value of an array with more than one element is ambiguous" during collection (via getfuncargnames).

Change: replaced the containment check with identity comparison — `any(p.new is sentinel for sentinel in sentinels)` — so no `__eq__` is ever invoked on the user-supplied `new` object. No `in`/`==` remains against `p.new`. Semantics otherwise unchanged: only patchings using the DEFAULT sentinel consume a mock argument, and the fallback path (mock/unittest.mock not imported) still returns len(patchings).

Files changed (3):
- src/_pytest/compat.py — the fix
- testing/test_compat.py — new regression tests: test_num_mock_patch_args_no_patchings (parametrized (), []) and test_num_mock_patch_args_with_new_array (a patching whose `new` has a truth-ambiguous `==` no longer raises; it is excluded, the DEFAULT patching still counts as 1, and getfuncargnames returns ())
- changelog/5631.bugfix.rst

My test evidence on this exact version: testing/test_compat.py -> 11 passed, 0 failed; testing/python/fixtures.py + testing/test_unittest.py with -k "mock or argnames or patch" -> 2 passed, 0 failed.

Suggested independent check: integrate patch-1, then run_testS on testing/test_compat.py. You may also want to confirm with a numpy-array reproduction, since the regression test uses a stand-in object rather than depending on numpy being installed. Please reply with accept or request_changes.

Review complete: patch-1 ACCEPTED (review-1, decision=accept).

How I verified (independent of your report):
- integrate_patch(patch-1) into my private tree -> version v2, files_sha256 eb6f7a08ddb7e492e733b39e55c84f409711cbc18afe65037f9a5e4178a9ee6a (no conflicts).
- Inspected the actual diff: src/_pytest/compat.py now uses `any(p.new is sentinel for sentinel in sentinels)` instead of `p.new in sentinels`. Semantics preserved: explicit `new` still consumes no fixture arg, `new=DEFAULT` still counts, no-patchings path unchanged. changelog/5631.bugfix.rst included, plus regression test in testing/test_compat.py.
- run_tests on that exact version (report test-report-5060b821c92b1cb7c7c5dd87): validation_status=verified, collected 30, passed 26, skipped 4, failed 0, errors 0.
  Passing nodes of interest: testing/test_compat.py::test_num_mock_patch_args_with_new_array, ::test_num_mock_patch_args_no_patchings[patchings0/patchings1], testing/python/integration.py::TestMockDecoration::test_wrapped_getfuncargnames, ::test_getfuncargnames_patching, ::test_unittest_mock, ::test_unittest_mock_and_fixture.

Two things for your delivery step:
1. A wider selection of mine that included testing/python/metafunc.py ended in a collection ImportError for the missing third-party module `hypothesis`. That is an environment limitation, not a defect of the patch; keep your final verification targets to ones that do not need hypothesis.
2. I saw deliveries already record delivery-1 for patch-1 (test_sequence 23). My acceptance is evidence only; it does not merge into your tree. Make sure your own final working tree integrates patch-1, has same-version run_tests passing, then fix_patch(task_ids=[]) and submit_integration as designated delivery member.

No changes requested. Nothing further needed from me unless you publish a revised candidate.

New final candidate: patch-2 (supersedes patch-1). Please integrate, run public tests on that exact version, then accept or request changes.

What changed vs patch-1
-----------------------
The src/_pytest/compat.py fix is IDENTICAL (identity test `any(p.new is sentinel for sentinel in sentinels)` replacing `p.new in sentinels`); patch-2 is patch-1 plus one additional regression test. If you already have patch-1 integrated, integrating patch-2 gives you the same source fix and the extra test.

Why the extra test
------------------
The issue's traceback is a *collection* error (python.py -> getfixtureinfo -> getfuncargnames -> num_mock_patch_args). patch-1's tests only called num_mock_patch_args/getfuncargnames directly. patch-2 adds:

  test_mock_patch_new_array_does_not_break_collection(testdir)
  - testdir.makepyfile writes a test decorated with @patch(target="os.getcwd", new=ArrayLike())
  - ArrayLike mimic numpy: __eq__/__ne__ return an object whose __bool__ raises ValueError("truth value is ambiguous")
  - asserts a nested runpytest() reports "1 passed" and exit code 0, i.e. no collection error.

Also included from patch-1: test_num_mock_patch_args_no_patchings (empty patchings -> 0) and test_num_mock_patch_args_with_new_array (one `new=<ambiguous-eq object>` patch + one `new=DEFAULT` patch -> num_mock_patch_args == 1, getfuncargnames == ()). No numpy dependency; runs anywhere.

How to reproduce the defect independently
-----------------------------------------
Stash/ignore the fix (or evaluate the old expression `p.new in sentinels` directly) and the end-to-end test fails with exactly the issue's ValueError; with the fix it passes. Note for your own check: with `new` explicitly given, unittest.mock leaves p.attribute_name as None for a dotted string target, so the `not p.attribute_name` guard does NOT short-circuit before the comparison — the comparison really is reached (I verified this empirically with a probe, correcting an earlier wrong assumption of mine).

Evidence on this exact version (v8, files_sha256 0ae9772daaceae82e9b4b5183a777becd79c0ba26d8493990c8e570d01b411f3)
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
run_tests(targets=["testing/test_compat.py"]) -> collected 12, passed 12, failed 0, errors 0; validation_status=verified. The nested session shows test_patched_with_array passing setup/call/teardown (exitstatus 0, collection_errors 0).
